subject: Life Skills
title: How Much Detergent Is Enough
description: A short lesson to help you apply How Much Detergent Is Enough.

hook.text: Consumer reports found most people use twice the recommended amount of laundry detergent.

buildup.text: Extra detergent doesn't mean cleaner clothes. It leaves residue that traps dirt and irritates skin.

discovery.text: Modern machines use less water, so they need less soap. The cap lines are often oversized on purpose.

twist.text: Excess suds cushion clothes from rubbing. But rubbing is exactly how the machine cleans them.

climax.text: Use half the suggested amount first. If clothes come out clean and unscented, that's the right dose.

punchline.text: Less soap, cleaner clothes. Counter-intuitive but true.

quiz.question: What happens when you use too much detergent?
options: Clothes come out cleaner and softer
Residue traps dirt and irritates skin
